arguments.content:
The Amazon Rainforest (Amazonia)

The Amazon Rainforest represents approximately one-quarter of the total area of remaining tropical forests on Earth. It is the largest tropical rainforest in the world, covering about 5.5 million square kilometers across nine South American countries, with the majority located in Brazil. The Amazon is also one of the most biodiverse regions on the planet, containing an estimated 10% of all species on Earth.
